statement: Of the various methods suggested for bleaching palm oil, the bichromate process originated by Watts is undoubtedly the best.
source_passage:
Of the various methods suggested for bleaching palm
oil, the bichromate process originated by Watts is undoubtedly the best.

statement: In bleaching palm oil with potassium bichromate and commercial muriatic acid, 22 to 28 lb. potassium bichromate and 45 to 60 lb. acid for every ton of oil will be found sufficient to produce a good bleached oil.
source_passage:
For every ton of oil, 22 to 28 lb. potassium
bichromate and 45 to 60 lb. acid will be found sufficient to produce a
good bleached oil.

statement: If the temperature is allowed to rise above 130 deg. F. (54 deg. C.) during the bleaching of palm oil, the resultant oil on saponification is apt to yield a soap of a "foxy" colour.
source_passage:
It is important, however, that the temperature should not be allowed to
rise above 130 deg. F. (54 deg. C.) during the bleaching of palm oil, otherwise
the resultant oil on saponification is apt to yield a soap of a "foxy"
colour.

statement: The deep colouring matter of crude cotton-seed oil, together with the mucilaginous and resinous principles, are removed by refining with caustic soda lye.
source_passage:
The deep colouring matter of crude cotton-seed
oil, together with the mucilaginous and resinous principles, are removed
by refining with caustic soda lye.

statement: In refining cotton-seed oil, prolonged agitation with air has a tendency to oxidise the oil, which increases its specific gravity and refractive index, and will be found in the soap-pan to produce a reddish soap.
source_passage:
Prolonged agitation with air has a tendency to oxidise the oil, which
increases its specific gravity and refractive index, and will be found
in the soap-pan to produce a reddish soap.

statement: The residue or "foots" produced during the refining of crude cotton-seed oil is known in the trade as "mucilage."
source_passage:
The residue or "foots" produced during the refining of crude
cotton-seed oil, known in the trade as "mucilage,"

statement: To remove a portion of the free fatty acids from a refined vegetable oil, it is sometimes only necessary to well agitate the oil with 1-1/2 per cent. of its weight of a 12 deg. Tw. (8 deg. B.) solution of caustic soda and allow to settle.
source_passage:
Sometimes it is only necessary to
well agitate the oil with 1-1/2 per cent. of its weight of a 12 deg. Tw. (8 deg.
B.) solution of caustic soda and allow to settle.

statement: Tallows are often greatly improved by alkaline treatment with a weak solution of caustic lye at 165 deg. F. (73 deg. C.).
source_passage:
Tallows are often greatly improved by the above alkaline
treatment at 165 deg. F. (73 deg. C.).

statement: For removing calcium (lime) salts from bone fat, hydrochloric acid is preferable to sulphuric acid, because the lime salt formed is readily soluble and easily removed.
source_passage:
These impurities must be removed
by a treatment with hydrochloric or sulphuric acid. The former acid is
preferable, as the lime salt formed is readily soluble and easily
removed.

statement: Rosin is converted into resinate of soda by heating 37 cwt. of 17 deg. Tw. (11 deg. B.) caustic soda lye, adding 20 cwt. of rosin broken into pieces, boiling until all the resinate is homogeneous, then adding 1-1/2 cwt. of salt and prolonging the boiling a little.
source_passage:
The process is commenced by heating 37 cwt. of 17 deg.
Tw. (11 deg. B.) caustic soda lye, and adding 20 cwt. of rosin, broken into
pieces, and continuing the boiling until all the resinate is
homogeneous, when an addition of 1-1/2 cwt. of salt is made and the
boiling prolonged a little.

statement: When rosin is treated with soda ash, frothing takes place owing to the liberation of CO_{2} gas.
source_passage:
Owing to the
liberation of CO_{2} gas, frothing takes place.

statement: Molten settled fatty materials en route to the soap-pan should be passed through sieves sufficiently fine to free them from suspended matter.
source_passage:
The molten
settled fatty materials _en route_ to the soap-pan should be passed
through sieves sufficiently fine to free them from suspended matter.
